numerical_failure.observed_behavior: Object-dtype array of numbers cast to timedelta64 with a unit is read as nanoseconds and truncated: pd.Series([2, 3], dtype=object).astype("m8[s]") returns [0 days, 0 days] (all zeros).
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: The numbers should be interpreted in the dtype's unit, matching pd.Series([2, 3], dtype="m8[s]"): [0:00:02, 0:00:03].
trigger_conditions: object-dtype input whose non-null values are all numbers
astype (or construction from existing object-dtype data) to a timedelta64 dtype with a unit such as m8[s]
reached via Series.astype, DataFrame.astype, Index.astype, and Series/DataFrame construction from object-dtype data
numbers such as -2 and 2**40 previously overflowed or floored in nanoseconds
oracle_clues: PR reproducer compares against pd.Series([2, 3], dtype="m8[s]") as the correct reference
fix is to delegate the timedelta64 branch to TimedeltaArray/_from_sequence like the datetime64 branch delegates to DatetimeArray._from_sequence
numeric-object results are expected to match to_timedelta(unit=...)

numerical_characteristics.precision: unit-level: requested unit s (seconds) or ms; passages state no explicit numeric precision beyond the unit
numerical_characteristics.magnitude: small integers 2, 3 (and 4, 5, 7); the bug treats bare numbers as nanoseconds, so 2 and 3 ns truncate to 0 days
category_specific_evidence: Constructor pd.Series([2, 3], dtype="m8[s]") gives [0:00:02, 0:00:03], the correct behavior
pd.Series([2, 3], dtype=object).astype("m8[s]") gives [0 days, 0 days], wrong: the numbers were read as nanoseconds and truncated
Commit: object-dtype astype to timedelta64 called array_to_timedelta64 with no unit and cast the nanosecond result to the requested dtype, so the unit was ignored
Expected invariant: astype on object input must agree with the constructor pd.Series(values, dtype="m8[ms]") (test_astype_object_to_timedelta64_unit_numeric_only)
Frame test: df.astype("m8[s]") on {'a': [2, 3], 'b': ['1 sec', '2 sec']} must equal pd.DataFrame(..., dtype="m8[s]"), and the column result must match df['a'].astype("m8[s]")
The unit applies only when every non-null entry is a bare number; mixed string/Timedelta entries must match the constructor
datetime64 branch delegating to DatetimeArray._from_sequence was already correct; timedelta64 should follow the same route
Object-to-datetimelike with no unit (m8, M8) should raise ValueError 'dtype with no precision is not allowed'
reproduction_risks: Block layout matters: a single-column and a multi-column object block take different paths, so the 2D case must be tested with both df[["a"]] and the full frame
A string column sharing a block with numeric column 'a' must not change how 'a' is read
Output shows 0 days for truncated values, so checking only the repr may miss the bug; compare values with assert_series_equal/assert_frame_equal
Unrelated passages (overflow sum, merge error message wording) are not part of this numerical reproduction
